When a page's job is to hold records that people or Claude will add to or change later — a tracker, a sign-up sheet, a log, a dashboard's numbers — Claude gives the page this database (the `db` capability, via the `artifact-capabilities` skill) instead of writing the records into the page source or browser storage, and later adds or changes rows with `ArtifactData` rather than republishing the page.

**Separate tools**: Claude handles comment threads on a published artifact with `ArtifactComments` and an artifact's shared database with `ArtifactData`, whose actions are what a skill or type instruction means by `read_db` or `write_db`. Claude loads either tool when it needs it, and if one appears only as a deferred tool's name, Claude loads it the way this session loads deferred tools before calling it.

**Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'pin', 'unpin'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

content.text:
I checked your workspace first. `C:\Users\Prateechi\enam` is an empty file, so we're starting from nothing. Python 3.12 and Node 22 are installed, which covers everything below. Your home folder is itself a git repo, so I'd put the project in its own repo at `C:\Users\Prateechi\finn`.

# FINN: product and technical plan

## 1. What the brief actually rewards

From the grading text, the priorities are:

1. **Judgment about filtering.** The brief says "surfacing the few things that actually matter and burying everything else." Ranking and collapsing routine filings matter more than showing everything.
2. **Analysing management, not summarising it.** The brief calls the promised-versus-delivered comparison "the kind of thing we value most." This should be the flagship.
3. **A clear point of view on interaction.** A chatbot plus a dashboard is the obvious answer they want us to move past.
4. **Getting the numbers right.** They're an investment firm. One made-up number in the demo undoes everything else.
5. **Cost discipline.** Model routing, caching and chunking earn bonus points.
6. **It runs.** "A demo that doesn't run is the worst outcome."

Two timing facts help us:
- **It's peak results season.** The Jul–Sep 2026 quarter results are being filed now (mid-Oct to mid-Nov), so the demo will have real, fresh results filings.
- **We have 6 days** (9–15 Nov). That's tight, so the scope has to be narrow.

## 2. Key product insight: three data shortcuts

Most entrants will run PDFs through an LLM and hope the numbers come out right. Three facts about Indian filings make a more accurate approach possible:

| Problem | Naive approach | Better approach |
|---|---|---|
| Quarterly results numbers | LLM reads the PDF | **Results filings in the standard SEBI format already contain three columns: this quarter, last quarter, and the same quarter last year.** One primary document gives both QoQ and YoY. Use the **XBRL** version (machine-readable, exact) where the exchange provides it, with PDF table parsing plus an LLM as fallback. |
| Bio of an incoming CFO or CEO | Scrape LinkedIn (against its terms, blocked, fragile) | **SEBI disclosure rules require a "brief profile" of any newly appointed director or key manager inside the filing itself.** Extract it from the filing, a primary source. Optionally add a clearly labelled web-search supplement. |
| Announcement classification | LLM on every filing | **BSE attaches its own category to each filing** (Result, Board Meeting, AGM/EGM, Insider Trading/SAST, and so on). Rules on the category and subject line should handle most filings for free. Only ambiguous ones go to a cheap model. |

**A strict rule for accuracy:** the LLM never produces a number. Numbers come from parsed tables and are computed in code. The LLM writes prose that refers to pre-computed facts by ID. A validator then checks that every number in the LLM's output exists in the fact table and rejects or regenerates the output if not. That's how we can honestly claim "no invented financial data."

**EBITDA is not reported directly.** We compute it as Revenue from operations − (Total expenses − Finance costs − Depreciation & amortisation), which excludes other income, and show that formula on the card. For **banks and NBFCs**, EBITDA doesn't apply. We show net interest income, operating profit, provisions and PAT instead, and label it that way. That's the kind of detail a finance reviewer will notice.

## 3. Recommended MVP

### Must have (the demo)

**Push: "The Brief"**
- A ranked feed of filings for any chosen window (24h by default, adjustable to 3d, 7d or custom).
- A **materiality score** that is deterministic and explainable: a base weight per category, adjusted for sub-type (a CFO exit outranks an independent-director exit; a rating downgrade outranks a reaffirmation), position weight in the portfolio, and same-day price reaction. Each card has a "Why is this ranked here?" explanation.
- Routine filings collapse into one line, for example "11 routine filings (ESOP allotments, compliance certificates)", which expands on tap.
- **Results card:** Revenue, EBITDA, PBT and PAT, each with QoQ and YoY, the margin change, a source chip linking to the filing page, and a confidence badge (arithmetic check: PBT − tax ≈ PAT).
- **Management-change card:** who left, who joined, and a profile extracted from the filing.
- Every other category gets a one-line "why it matters" summary, or no summary when a summary would add nothing.
- **End-of-day alerts:** configurable per stock or globally. Volume as a multiple of its 20-day average (default 2×), and price move as ±X% or in standard deviations of the stock's own volatility. A 3% move means different things for a utility and a small-cap.
- **Linking:** if a volume spike and a filing happen on the same day, they become one story ("Volume 3.4× — results filed 15:42").

**Pull: "The Research Memo"**
- Works for any NSE ticker. The pipeline is generic: symbol → screener page → filing documents.
- **Deterministic sections** (from screener's standardised tables, cross-checked against filings): financial snapshot, multi-year trajectory, balance sheet (debt-to-equity, working-capital days), and cash quality (cash from operations vs PAT, free cash flow). These render in seconds with no LLM cost.
- **Flagship: the "Promise Ledger."** Extract every guidance statement from the last 4 concall transcripts, each with a quote, quarter and page. Match each one against what was actually reported and give a verdict:
  - Delivered
  - Missed
  - Goalposts moved
  - **Silently dropped** (guidance that simply stopped being mentioned)

  The last verdict is the real analytical insight; summarisers can't produce it.
- **Bull vs bear:** three points each, every point with a citation chip that opens the source quote and page.
- Progressive rendering: the numbers appear first, and LLM-written sections stream in after.

**Mobile**
- An installable web app (PWA) with bottom navigation (Brief / Alerts / Research / Settings), built for one-handed use.

### Should have, if time allows (in this order)
1. Real phone notifications for triggered alerts via Web Push. This works on Android, and on iOS 16.4+ once the app is installed to the home screen.
2. **"Ask"**: free-form questions grounded only in that company's documents, with citations, and a refusal when the sources don't cover the question.
3. A 60-second audio version of the brief using the browser's built-in text-to-speech (free, and it covers the voice option the brief suggests).
4. Swipe gestures: swipe left to mute this category for this stock, swipe right to research it. This is the "inbox triage" interaction.

### Deliberately left out
- Intraday or real-time prices (the brief says end-of-day).
- User accounts and multiple users (one demo portfolio).
- News, broker notes and macro data (the brief forbids secondary sources on the pull side).
- Full RAG over 300-page annual reports (see section 5).
- A native app.

## 4. Interaction model: inbox triage, not a dashboard

The point of view to put in the writeup: **an investor's day is triage, so FINN works like an inbox you can clear in two minutes.** Opening the app shows "3 things matter today," ranked with reasons. Everything else is folded away. Every card is a doorway into research: tapping "Ask about this" on a results card opens that company's memo already scrolled to the Promise Ledger, so the reader can see "they said 15% growth; they delivered 9%." Push and pull are one continuous flow, not two separate tabs.

## 5. Architecture

```
            ┌───────────── Scheduled jobs (GitHub Actions cron, or local) ────────────┐
            │  every 30 min: BSE/NSE announcements → classify → score → enrich        │
            │  ~18:30 IST:   EOD prices (yfinance, fallback NSE bhavcopy) → alerts    │
            └──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                           ▼
 Exchange PDFs/XBRL ─► Ingestion & parsing (pdfplumber/PyMuPDF, XBRL parser)
 screener.in       ─►        │  content-hash every document → cache extractions forever
                             ▼
                ┌──── Postgres (Supabase/Neon free tier; SQLite in development) ────┐
                │ companies · prices_eod · announcements · documents · facts        │
                │ guidance_items · alerts · alert_rules · extractions · llm_ledger  │
                └──────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
              FastAPI (Python) ── model router ──┬─ rules (free)
                 │  REST + SSE streaming         ├─ cheap model: classification, extraction
                 │                               └─ strong model: Promise Ledger, bull/bear
                 ▼
         Next.js PWA (Vercel) ── Web Push (VAPID) ──► phone
```

**Data flow for a push item:** cron fetches new filings → deduplicate by exchange ID → rule classifier (cheap-model fallback) → materiality score → for high-materiality types, download the PDF or XBRL, hash it, extract structured JSON once, and validate it → store → if it crosses a user's alert rule, send a Web Push → the feed reads only from the database. The demo never depends on a live scrape.

**Data flow for a pull request:**
1. Resolve the ticker.
2. Fetch the screener financial tables and the list of documents. Cache both.
3. Render the deterministic sections immediately.
4. Run a per-transcript structured extraction (guidance statements, quote, page). This is a map step on a cheap model, cached by document hash.
5. Run one strong-model reasoning call over the extracted JSON plus the fact table to build the ledger and bull/bear.
6. Validate citations and numbers.
7. Stream the result to the client.

**Why per-document extraction instead of RAG:** a transcript is about 15–25k tokens and fits in context whole. Extracting it once into structured guidance items is cheaper, more complete (RAG misses guidance phrased unexpectedly), and reusable across every later question. Embeddings, using a free local model, are only needed for the "Ask" feature.

**Stack**

| Layer | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | Python + FastAPI | yfinance, PDF and XBRL tooling are all Python |
| Frontend | Next.js + Tailwind + PWA | Easiest for reviewers to open on a phone; free Vercel hosting |
| Database | Postgres (Neon/Supabase free) | Free tier; SQLite locally |
| Backend hosting | Fly.io or Render | Render's free tier sleeps (~50s cold start), so we keep it warm before the demo or use Fly |
| Bulk LLM work | Cheap/free model (Gemini Flash free tier, a Groq-hosted Llama, or Claude Haiku 5.5) | Classification and extraction |
| Reasoning LLM | Claude Sonnet 5.5 (or the best free option you have) | Only for the ledger and bull/bear |
| Cost visibility | `llm_ledger` table with tokens and cost per call, plus cache-hit rate, shown in the app and README | Makes the efficiency bonus visible |

## 6. Risks and data availability

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| NSE's API needs a cookie handshake and often blocks cloud IPs | High | BSE is the primary source (more tolerant with proper headers); NSE is secondary. Run ingestion from a local machine or cron and write to the hosted DB. Verify on day 1. |
| GitHub Actions IPs may also be blocked | Medium | Fallback: run ingestion locally on a schedule during the demo week |
| yfinance breaks or gets rate-limited | Medium | NSE bhavcopy (the official daily price file) as fallback; cache all history |
| Scanned or image-only PDFs | Medium | Prefer XBRL. Use OCR only as a last resort; otherwise mark the item "manual review" rather than guess |
| Standalone vs consolidated numbers mixed up | High (accuracy) | Always choose consolidated, label it on the card, cross-check against screener's quarterly table |
| Screener rate limits or terms | Medium | Polite fetching, aggressive caching, fetch only on demand; use company investor-relations pages as fallback |
| Not enough concall transcripts for small companies | Medium | Show "insufficient sources" honestly instead of a hollow ledger |
| Ticker changes after demergers or renames (e.g. Tata Motors, Zomato→Eternal, ITC Hotels) | Low | Avoid these in the demo portfolio; validate every ticker on day 1 |
| LLM hallucinating numbers or citations | High | Numeric-grounding validator plus a check that every quoted text actually appears on the cited page |
| Cold start or downtime during review | High | Keep the backend warm; fall back to a seeded database snapshot; record a demo video as backup |
| LinkedIn bios | — | Not promised. We use the profile required in the filing. I won't claim a LinkedIn integration we don't have. |

## 7. Portfolio (candidates, to be validated on day 1)

The aim is a spread of sectors and sizes, including types that stress-test the logic: banks (no EBITDA), lenders, companies with lots of filings, and small, volatile names.

- Large caps: RELIANCE, HDFCBANK, INFY, BAJFINANCE, SUNPHARMA, MARUTI, LT, ASIANPAINT, TITAN, BHARTIARTL
- Mid and smaller caps: DIXON, POLYCAB, PERSISTENT, TRENT, HAL, IRCTC, DEEPAKNTR, PAYTM, SUZLON
- On-demand research demos (outside the portfolio): PIDILITIND, KPITTECH, plus one that you pick live to show it generalises.

## 8. Day-by-day plan

| Day | Deliverable |
|---|---|
| **9–10 Nov** | Data checks with a go/no-go per source: BSE/NSE announcements, XBRL availability, yfinance or bhavcopy, the screener documents list, and parsing 3 results filings and 3 transcripts. Database schema and ingestion. |
| **11 Nov** | Push backend: classifier, materiality score, results extraction with validation, management profile extraction, end-of-day alert engine. |
| **12 Nov** | Pull backend: deterministic sections, transcript guidance extraction, Promise Ledger, bull/bear with citations, number and citation validators. |
| **13 Nov** | Frontend: the Brief feed, cards, alerts, settings and thresholds. |
| **14 Nov** | Frontend: research memo, citation viewer, streaming. Deploy. Web Push if time allows. |
| **15 Nov** | **Accuracy check:** hand-verify about 10 results extractions and 30 classifications and publish the accuracy figures in the README. Then the writeup, a demo video, and exporting the AI build history. |

The accuracy check is cheap and is the strongest signal we can give an AI-engineering reviewer.

## 9. Decisions I need from you before I start

1. **LLM access:** which API keys do you have or can you get (Gemini free tier, Groq, Anthropic, OpenAI)? This sets the routing.
2. **Deployment accounts:** do you have GitHub, Vercel, and one of Neon/Supabase and Fly/Render? Can a scheduled job run from your laptop during the week if exchange sites block cloud IPs?
3. **Scope:** are you happy with the Must list plus the Promise Ledger as the flagship, with Web Push as the first stretch goal?
4. **Portfolio:** keep my candidate list, or do you have your own picks?
5. **Location:** is a new repo at `C:\Users\Prateechi\finn` fine?

Once you approve, I'll start with the day-1 data checks and report exactly which sources work before building anything on top of them. I can also publish this plan as a shareable page if you want to keep it as a reference or adapt parts of it for your writeup.

"""Spike 1: EOD price/volume availability (yfinance primary, NSE bhavcopy fallback)."""
import datetime as dt
import io
import zipfile

import requests
import yfinance as yf

TICKERS = ["RELIANCE", "HDFCBANK", "DIXON", "SUZLON", "PAYTM"]

df = yf.download([t + ".NS" for t in TICKERS], period="1mo", interval="1d",
                 group_by="ticker", auto_adjust=False, progress=False)
for t in TICKERS:
    sub = df[t + ".NS"].dropna()
    print(f"yf {t:10s} rows={len(sub)} last={sub.index[-1].date()} close={sub['Close'].iloc[-1]:.2f} vol={int(sub['Volume'].iloc[-1])}")

UA = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 Chrome/124 Safari/537.36"}
d = dt.date.today()
for _ in range(7):
    d -= dt.timedelta(days=1)
    url = f"https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/cm/BhavCopy_NSE_CM_0_0_0_{d:%Y%m%d}_F_0000.csv.zip"
    r = requests.get(url, headers=UA, timeout=20)
    print("bhav", d, r.status_code, len(r.content))
    if r.status_code == 200:
        z = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(r.content))
        txt = z.read(z.namelist()[0]).decode()
        print(txt.splitlines()[0][:300])
        print(next(l for l in txt.splitlines() if ",RELIANCE," in l)[:300])
        break

"""Spike 2: corporate announcements from BSE and NSE."""
import datetime as dt
import json

import requests

UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0 Safari/537.36"

# --- BSE ---
s = requests.Session()
s.headers.update({"User-Agent": UA, "Referer": "https://www.bseindia.com/", "Origin": "https://www.bseindia.com",
                  "Accept": "application/json, text/plain, */*"})
to = dt.date.today()
fr = to - dt.timedelta(days=3)
url = ("https://api.bseindia.com/BseIndiaAPI/api/AnnSubCategoryGetData/w"
       f"?pageno=1&strCat=-1&strPrevDate={fr:%Y%m%d}&strScrip=500325&strSearch=P&strToDate={to:%Y%m%d}&strType=C&subcategory=-1")
r = s.get(url, timeout=20)
print("BSE scrip", r.status_code, r.headers.get("content-type"), len(r.content))
try:
    j = r.json()
    rows = j.get("Table", [])
    print("rows", len(rows))
    if rows:
        print(json.dumps(rows[0], indent=1)[:1500])
except Exception as e:

"""Spike 3: NSE results XBRL parse + NSE windowed announcements + screener.in page."""
import collections
import re

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from lxml import etree

UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0 Safari/537.36"
n = requests.Session()
n.headers.update({"User-Agent": UA, "Accept": "*/*", "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9", "Referer": "https://www.nseindia.com/"})
n.get("https://www.nseindia.com/", timeout=20)

for sym in ["RELIANCE", "HDFCBANK"]:
    res = n.get(f"https://www.nseindia.com/api/corporates-financial-results?index=equities&symbol={sym}&period=Quarterly", timeout=20).json()
    res.sort(key=lambda x: x["toDate"][-4:] + {"Mar": "03", "Jun": "06", "Sep": "09", "Dec": "12"}[x["toDate"][3:6]] + x["consolidated"], reverse=True)
    for x in res[:4]:
        print(sym, x["toDate"], x["consolidated"], x["bank"], x["filingDate"], x["xbrl"][-40:])
    latest = next(x for x in res if x["consolidated"] == "Consolidated")
    xml = n.get(latest["xbrl"], timeout=30).content
    root = etree.fromstring(xml)
    ctx = {}
    for c in root.iter("{*}context"):
        start = c.find(".//{*}startDate")
        end = c.find(".//{*}endDate")
        inst = c.find(".//{*}instant")
        dims = [m.text for m in c.iter("{*}explicitMember")]
        ctx[c.get("id")] = (start.text if start is not None else None, end.text if end is not None else (inst.text if inst is not None else None), dims)
    facts = collections.defaultdict(dict)
    for el in root:
        if not isinstance(el.tag, str) or el.get("contextRef") is None:
            continue
        name = etree.QName(el).localname
        s, e, dims = ctx.get(el.get("contextRef"), (None, None, None))
        if dims:
            continue
        facts[name][f"{s}..{e}"] = el.text
    print(sym, "fact names:", len(facts))
    for k in ["RevenueFromOperations", "OtherIncome", "Income", "Expenses", "FinanceCosts", "DepreciationDepletionAndAmortisationExpense",
              "ProfitBeforeTax", "TaxExpense", "ProfitLossForPeriod", "ProfitLossForPeriodFromContinuingOperations",
              "InterestEarned", "OperatingProfitBeforeProvisionAndContingencies", "ProvisionsOtherThanTaxAndContingencies",
              "BasicEarningsLossPerShareFromContinuingAndDiscontinuedOperations", "DateOfStartOfReportingPeriod", "WhetherResultsAreAuditedOrUnaudited"]:
        if k in facts:
            print("   ", k, dict(facts[k]))
    print("   sample names:", sorted(facts)[:60])

import collections, requests
from lxml import etree

n = requests.Session(); n.headers.update({"User-Agent": UA, "Referer": "https://www.nseindia.com/"})
n.get("https://www.nseindia.com/", timeout=20)

    root = etree.fromstring(n.get(x["xbrl"], timeout=30).content)
    ctx = {}
    for c in root.iter("{*}context"):
        g = lambda t: (c.find(f".//{{*}}{t}").text if c.find(f".//{{*}}{t}") is not None else None)
        ctx[c.get("id")] = (g("startDate"), g("endDate") or g("instant"), [m.text for m in c.iter("{*}explicitMember")])
    f = collections.defaultdict(dict)
    for el in root:
        if isinstance(el.tag, str) and el.get("contextRef"):
            s, e, d = ctx[el.get("contextRef")]
            if not d: f[etree.QName(el).localname][f"{s}..{e}"] = el.text
    print("  periods:", sorted({k for v in f.values() for k in v})[:10])
    for k in ["RevenueFromOperations","Expenses","FinanceCosts","DepreciationDepletionAndAmortisationExpense","ProfitBeforeTax","ProfitLossForPeriod","InterestEarned","InterestExpended","OperatingProfitBeforeProvisionAndContingencies","ProvisionsOtherThanTaxAndContingencies","ProfitLossFromOrdinaryActivitiesBeforeTax","ProfitLossForThePeriod","LevelOfRoundingUsedInFinancialStatements","NatureOfReportStandaloneConsolidated"]:

EOF

# FINN — data findings & decision log

A running record of what we verified, what we chose, and why. Dates are IST.

## 2026-11-09 — Day-1 data checks (scripts in `spikes/`)

| # | Source | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| s1 | yfinance `.NS` EOD | Works: same-day close + volume for all 19 tickers | Primary price source |
| s1 | NSE bhavcopy (`BhavCopy_NSE_CM_…csv.zip`) | Works, full-market daily file | Fallback price source |
| s2 | BSE `AnnSubCategoryGetData` | Works per scrip code; returns `CATEGORYNAME` + `SUBCATNAME` | Fallback announcement source |
| s2 | NSE `corporate-announcements` | Works after a cookie handshake from a residential IP; returns `desc` (≈40 distinct exchange categories), the attachment PDF URL and a summary sentence | **Primary announcement source** |
| s3 | NSE `corporates-financial-results` XBRL | Ends Dec-2024 — SEBI moved results to Integrated Filing | Used only for pre-2025 quarters |
| s4/5 | NSE `integrated-filing-results` XBRL | Current quarter + YTD, exact rupee values, both Ind-AS and banking taxonomies | **Primary source for the results card** |
| s3 | screener.in company page (no login) | 13 quarters, 12 yrs P&L/BS/CF, working-capital ratios, AR + concall transcript links (BSE-hosted PDFs) | Pull-side financials + document discovery; cross-check for results |
| s4 | BSE transcript PDF via PyMuPDF | Text layer present: 24 pages / ~16k tokens for DIXON Q2 FY27 | Whole-document extraction fits in one context window → no RAG needed for the ledger |
| s6 | 19-ticker portfolio | All resolve on all three sources | Portfolio confirmed |

### Notable findings
- **Sources lag each other.** On 9 Nov, screener still showed Jun-2026 for HAL and IRCTC while NSE XBRL had Sep-2026; for INFY it was the reverse. The results card therefore uses XBRL first, falls back to screener, and shows which one it used.
- **Banks use a different taxonomy** (`InterestEarned`, `OperatingProfitBeforeProvisionAndContingencies`, …). EBITDA does not apply; bank cards show NII / pre-provision operating profit / provisions / PAT instead.
- **EBITDA is never reported directly.** We compute it as `Revenue from ops − (Total expenses − Finance costs − D&A)`, which excludes other income. This matches screener's "Operating Profit", so the two sources can be cross-checked.
- **Cloud IP risk:** NSE sits behind Akamai bot protection. Ingestion is designed to run wherever NSE answers (laptop or CI) and write to the shared database, so the hosted API never depends on scraping NSE live.

## Architecture decisions
- **Frontend: Vite + React + TypeScript (static PWA on Vercel)** instead of Next.js. All data comes from the API, so server rendering adds nothing; a static bundle has fewer deploy failure modes.
- **LLM layer is provider-agnostic** (OpenAI-compatible chat API). Routing by task tier:
  - `rules` (free): exchange category → our category for most filings.
  - `fast` (Groq free tier / Gemini Flash-Lite): ambiguous classification, one-line "why it matters".
  - `long` (Gemini Flash, large context): one-time structured extraction per transcript / filing PDF, cached by content hash.
  - `reason` (best available): Promise Ledger verdicts and bull/bear over *extracted JSON*, not raw documents.
  - Ollama (`gemma3:4b`, local) as the offline dev fallback.
- **The LLM never produces numbers.** Figures come from XBRL/screener tables computed in code. LLM prose cites fact IDs; a validator rejects any number not in the fact table, and any quote not found verbatim (after whitespace normalisation) on the cited page.
- **Cache everything by content hash**: PDFs, page text, extractions, LLM responses. Every LLM call is logged to `llm_ledger` (tokens, latency, cache hit) and shown in the app.

content.text: Next I'll pull two weeks of NSE filings across the whole market. That shows every exchange category the classifier has to map, using real data rather than guesses.

input.command:
cd /c/Users/Prateechi/finn && uv pip install --python backend/.venv/Scripts/python.exe sqlalchemy "psycopg[binary]" 2>&1 | tail -1; cat > spikes/s7_categories.py <<'EOF'
"""Spike 7: enumerate NSE announcement categories (desc) over 2 weeks with a sample each."""
import collections, json, requests
UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0 Safari/537.36"
n = requests.Session(); n.headers.update({"User-Agent": UA, "Referer": "https://www.nseindia.com/"}); n.get("https://www.nseindia.com/", timeout=20)
rows = []
for fr, to in [("26-10-2026", "01-11-2026"), ("02-11-2026", "09-11-2026")]:
    rows += n.get(f"https://www.nseindia.com/api/corporate-announcements?index=equities&from_date={fr}&to_date={to}", timeout=60).json()
c = collections.Counter(r["desc"] for r in rows)
sample = {}

import datetime as dt
import json
from contextlib import contextmanager

from sqlalchemy import (JSON, Boolean, Date, DateTime, Float, Integer, String, Text, create_engine, select)
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, sessionmaker

from .config import DATABASE_URL, DEFAULT_SETTINGS

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, pool_pre_ping=True,
                       connect_args={"check_same_thread": False} if DATABASE_URL.startswith("sqlite") else {})
Session = sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


def now() -> dt.datetime:
    return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)


class Company(Base):
    __tablename__ = "companies"
    symbol: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(200))
    sector: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))
    bse_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(16))
    in_portfolio: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)
    weight: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float, default=0.0)  # % of mock portfolio value


class PriceEOD(Base):
    __tablename__ = "prices_eod"
    symbol: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), primary_key=True)
    date: Mapped[dt.date] = mapped_column(Date, primary_key=True)
    open: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float)
    high: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float)
    low: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float)
    close: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float)
    volume: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float)


class Announcement(Base):
    __tablename__ = "announcements"
    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64), primary_key=True)  # "NSE:<seq_id>" / "BSE:<newsid>"
    symbol: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), index=True)
    ts: Mapped[dt.datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime, index=True)  # IST, naive
    exch_category: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(200))
    text: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    pdf_url: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(500))
    category: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(40), index=True)
    classified_by: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(20))
    materiality: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, default=0)
    reasons: Mapped[list] = mapped_column(JSON, default=list)
    summary: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    enrichment: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(JSON)
    enriched_at: Mapped[dt.datetime | None] = mapped_column(DateTime)


class Alert(Base):
    __tablename__ = "alerts"
    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120), primary_key=True)  # deterministic -> idempotent
    symbol: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), index=True)
    kind: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20))  # price | volume | announcement
    date: Mapped[dt.date] = mapped_column(Date, index=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(300))
    detail: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(JSON, default=dict)
    created_at: Mapped[dt.datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime, default=now)


class KV(Base):
    """Generic cache / settings store: http bodies, pdf text, llm responses, research reports."""
    __tablename__ = "kv"
    key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(300), primary_key=True)
    value: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text)
    updated_at: Mapped[dt.datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime, default=now)


class LLMCall(Base):
    __tablename__ = "llm_calls"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    ts: Mapped[dt.datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime, default=now)
    task: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(60))
    provider: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(30))
    model: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100))
    tokens_in: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, default=0)
    tokens_out: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, default=0)
    ms: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, default=0)
    cache_hit: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)
    ok: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True)


def init_db():
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)


@contextmanager
def session():
    s = Session()
    try:
        yield s
        s.commit()
    except Exception:
        s.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        s.close()


def kv_get(key: str, max_age: dt.timedelta | None = None):
    with session() as s:
        row = s.get(KV, key)
        if row is None or (max_age and now() - row.updated_at > max_age):
            return None
        return json.loads(row.value)


def kv_set(key: str, value) -> None:
    with session() as s:
        s.merge(KV(key=key, value=json.dumps(value, default=str), updated_at=now()))


def get_settings() -> dict:
    return {**DEFAULT_SETTINGS, **(kv_get("settings") or {})}


def portfolio_symbols() -> list[str]:
    with session() as s:
        return list(s.scalars(select(Company.symbol).where(Company.in_portfolio)))

"""Provider-agnostic LLM router.

Every provider speaks the OpenAI chat-completions dialect, so routing is just (base_url, key, model).
Tasks ask for a *tier*; the router walks that tier's candidates and skips providers without a key or
that fail (rate limit, outage). Responses are cached by a hash of (model, messages) and every call is
logged to llm_calls so cost and cache-hit rate are visible.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import time

import httpx

from .db import LLMCall, kv_get, kv_set, session

PROVIDERS = {
    "gemini": ("https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai", "GEMINI_API_KEY"),
    "groq": ("https://api.groq.com/openai/v1", "GROQ_API_KEY"),
    "openrouter": ("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"),
    "openai": ("https://api.openai.com/v1", "OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    "ollama": (os.getenv("OLLAMA_URL", "http://localhost:11434") + "/v1", None),
}

# Ordered candidates per tier. Override any model with env FINN_MODEL_<PROVIDER>_<TIER>.
TIERS = {
    # short inputs, high volume: classification fallback, one-liners, profile extraction
    "fast": [("groq", "llama-3.1-8b-instant"), ("gemini", "gemini-2.5-flash-lite"),
             ("openrouter", "meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free"), ("openai", "gpt-4o-mini"), ("ollama", "gemma3:4b")],
    # whole documents (~20k tokens): transcript guidance extraction
    "long": [("gemini", "gemini-2.5-flash"), ("gemini", "gemini-2.5-flash-lite"),
             ("openrouter", "google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free"), ("openai", "gpt-4o-mini"), ("ollama", "gemma3:4b")],
    # reasoning over extracted JSON: promise-ledger verdicts, bull/bear
    "reason": [("gemini", "gemini-2.5-flash"), ("groq", "openai/gpt-oss-120b"), ("groq", "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"),
               ("openrouter", "deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324:free"), ("openai", "gpt-4o-mini"), ("ollama", "gemma3:4b")],
}


class LLMUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    pass


def _key(provider: str) -> str | None:
    env = PROVIDERS[provider][1]
    if env is None:
        return "ollama" if os.getenv("FINN_USE_OLLAMA") == "1" else None
    return os.getenv(env)


def available() -> dict:
    return {t: [f"{p}:{os.getenv(f'FINN_MODEL_{p.upper()}_{t.upper()}', m)}" for p, m in c if _key(p)] for t, c in TIERS.items()}


def _log(**kw):
    try:
        with session() as s:
            s.add(LLMCall(**kw))
    except Exception:
        pass


def _parse_json(text: str):
    text = text.strip()
    m = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)```", text, re.S)
    if m:
        text = m.group(1)
    start = min([i for i in (text.find("{"), text.find("[")) if i >= 0], default=0)
    return json.loads(text[start:])


def chat_json(task: str, tier: str, system: str, user: str, max_tokens: int = 2000, temperature: float = 0.1):
    """Return parsed JSON from the first working candidate of `tier`."""
    errors = []
    for provider, model in TIERS[tier]:
        key = _key(provider)
        if not key:
            continue
        model = os.getenv(f"FINN_MODEL_{provider.upper()}_{tier.upper()}", model)
        ck = "llm:" + hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([model, system, user]).encode()).hexdigest()
        if (hit := kv_get(ck)) is not None:
            _log(task=task, provider=provider, model=model, cache_hit=True)
            return hit
        base = PROVIDERS[provider][0]
        body = {"model": model, "temperature": temperature, "max_tokens": max_tokens,
                "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
                "response_format": {"type": "json_object"}}
        if provider == "groq" and "gpt-oss" in model:
            body["reasoning_effort"] = "medium"
        t0 = time.time()

    ("management_change", r"re-?appoint", -15, "Re-appointment, not a change"),
    ("credit_rating", r"downgrad|negative|watch with negative", 45, "Rating downgrade / negative outlook"),

    ("credit_rating", r"reaffirm|re-affirm|retained", -20, "Rating reaffirmed — no change"),
    ("credit_rating", r"withdraw", -15, "Rating withdrawn (often debt repaid)"),
    ("litigation", r"insolvency|nclt|fraud|forensic|default|arrest|search|seizure", 22, "Insolvency / fraud / default signal"),
    ("litigation", r"penalty of rs\.? ?[0-9,]{1,7}(\.\d+)?/?-? |no material impact|not material", -30, "Company says impact is immaterial"),
    ("M&A", r"incorporat|name change|strike[- ]off", -45, "Subsidiary housekeeping, not a deal"),
    ("M&A", r"completion|completed|consummat", -10, "Completion of a previously announced deal"),
    ("M&A", r"open offer|demerg|amalgamat|merger", 10, "Structural change to the company"),

]

def tier(score: int) -> str:
    return "critical" if score >= 75 else "notable" if score >= 45 else "routine"


def score(category: str, exch_category: str, text: str, weight: float = 0.0, price_move_pct: float | None = None,
          move_threshold: float = 4.0) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    s = BASE.get(category, 10)
    reasons = [f"{category.replace('_', ' ')} base {s}"]
    blob = f"{exch_category} {text}"
    for c, rx, adj, why in _ADJ:
        if c == category and rx.search(blob):
            s += adj
            reasons.append(f"{why} ({adj:+d})")
    if weight and s >= 30:

            s += bump

        s += 10
        reasons.append(f"Stock moved {price_move_pct:+.1f}% that day (+10)")
    return max(0, min(100, s)), reasons

"""Triggered alerts, evaluated on read against the user's current thresholds.

Price: |daily return| ≥ X%  (also reports the move in σ of the stock's own recent volatility)
Volume: volume ≥ k × trailing N-day average
Announcement: category in the user's watch-list and materiality ≥ threshold
Price/volume alerts are linked to a same-session filing when one exists — "volume 3× · results filed 15:42".
"""
import datetime as dt
import statistics

from sqlalchemy import select

from ..db import Announcement, Company, session
from ..sources.prices import history

MARKET_CLOSE = dt.time(15, 30)


def _session_date(ts: dt.datetime, trading_days: list[dt.date]) -> dt.date | None:
    """The trading session in which the market could first react to a filing made at `ts`."""
    d = ts.date() if ts.time() < MARKET_CLOSE else ts.date() + dt.timedelta(days=1)
    for t in trading_days:
        if t >= d:
            return t
    return None


def eod_moves(symbol: str, settings: dict, days: int = 7) -> list[dict]:
    override = (settings.get("overrides") or {}).get(symbol, {})
    pct_th = override.get("price_move_pct", settings["price_move_pct"])
    vol_th = override.get("volume_multiple", settings["volume_multiple"])
    look = settings["volume_lookback_days"]
    rows = history(symbol, look + days + 5)
    out = []
    for i in range(max(look + 1, len(rows) - days), len(rows)):
        cur, prev = rows[i], rows[i - 1]
        window = rows[i - look:i]
        rets = [window[j].close / window[j - 1].close - 1 for j in range(1, len(window))]
        sigma = statistics.pstdev(rets) if len(rets) > 5 else None
        ret = cur.close / prev.close - 1
        avg_vol = statistics.fmean([w.volume for w in window if w.volume]) if window else None
        mult = cur.volume / avg_vol if avg_vol and cur.volume else None
        z = ret / sigma if sigma else None
        base = {"symbol": symbol, "date": cur.date.isoformat(), "close": round(cur.close, 2),
                "ret_pct": round(ret * 100, 2), "sigma": round(z, 1) if z is not None else None,
                "vol_mult": round(mult, 2) if mult else None, "volume": cur.volume}
        if abs(ret) * 100 >= pct_th:
            out.append({**base, "kind": "price", "threshold": pct_th,
                        "title": f"{symbol} {ret * 100:+.1f}% to ₹{cur.close:,.2f}"
                                 + (f" · {abs(z):.1f}σ move" if z is not None else "")})
        if mult and mult >= vol_th:
            out.append({**base, "kind": "volume", "threshold": vol_th,
                        "title": f"{symbol} volume {mult:.1f}× its {look}-day average"
                                 + f" · price {ret * 100:+.1f}%"})
    return out


def compute(settings: dict, days: int = 7) -> list[dict]:
    with session() as s:
        symbols = list(s.scalars(select(Company.symbol).where(Company.in_portfolio)))
        since = dt.datetime.now() - dt.timedelta(days=days + 3)
        anns = list(s.scalars(select(Announcement).where(Announcement.ts >= since, Announcement.symbol.in_(symbols))))
    alerts = []
    for sym in symbols:
        trading = [r.date for r in history(sym, 40)]
        moves = eod_moves(sym, settings, days)
        sym_anns = [a for a in anns if a.symbol == sym and a.materiality >= 25]
        for m in moves:
            d = dt.date.fromisoformat(m["date"])
            linked = [a for a in sym_anns if _session_date(a.ts, trading) == d]
            linked.sort(key=lambda a: -a.materiality)
            if linked:
                a = linked[0]
                m["linked"] = {"id": a.id, "category": a.category, "ts": a.ts.isoformat(), "text": a.summary or a.text}
            m["id"] = f"{m['kind']}:{sym}:{m['date']}"
            alerts.append(m)
    cutoff = dt.datetime.now() - dt.timedelta(days=days)
    for a in anns:
        if a.ts >= cutoff and a.category in settings["alert_categories"] and a.materiality >= settings["min_alert_materiality"]:
            alerts.append({"id": f"ann:{a.id}", "kind": "announcement", "symbol": a.symbol, "date": a.ts.date().isoformat(),
                           "ts": a.ts.isoformat(), "category": a.category, "materiality": a.materiality,
                           "title": f"{a.symbol} · {a.category.replace('_', ' ')}", "announcement_id": a.id,
                           "text": a.summary or a.text})
    alerts.sort(key=lambda x: (x["date"], x.get("ts", "")), reverse=True)
    return alerts

"""Push pipeline: fetch → classify → score → enrich. Idempotent; safe to run on a schedule."""
import datetime as dt
import json

from sqlalchemy import select

from ..config import BACKEND
from ..db import Announcement, Company, get_settings, now, portfolio_symbols, session
from ..sources import docs, nse, prices, screener
from . import classify, enrich, score
from .alerts import _session_date

PORTFOLIO_FILE = BACKEND / "portfolio.json"


def load_portfolio() -> list[str]:
    spec = json.loads(PORTFOLIO_FILE.read_text())
    with session() as s:
        for row in s.scalars(select(Company)):
            row.in_portfolio = False
        for p in spec["holdings"]:
            c = s.get(Company, p["symbol"]) or Company(symbol=p["symbol"])
            c.in_portfolio, c.weight = True, p["weight"]
            c.sector = p.get("sector") or c.sector
            s.merge(c)
    for p in spec["holdings"]:
        with session() as s:
            c = s.get(Company, p["symbol"])
            if not c.name:
                try:
                    sc = screener.company(p["symbol"])
                    c.name, c.bse_code = sc["name"], sc["bse_code"]
                except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                    print("screener meta failed", p["symbol"], e)
    return [p["symbol"] for p in spec["holdings"]]


def _price_move(symbol: str, ts: dt.datetime) -> float | None:
    rows = prices.history(symbol, 60)
    days = [r.date for r in rows]
    d = _session_date(ts, days)
    if d is None:
        return None
    i = days.index(d)
    return (rows[i].close / rows[i - 1].close - 1) * 100 if i > 0 else None


def process(a: Announcement, weight: float, settings: dict, use_llm: bool = True):
    cat, how = classify.rule_classify(a.exch_category, a.text)
    if cat is None and a.pdf_url:  # peek at the document before paying for an LLM call
        try:
            first = " ".join(docs.pages(a.pdf_url, max_pages=2)["pages"])[:4000]
            cat, how = classify.rule_classify(a.exch_category, f"{a.text} {first}")
            how = "rule+pdf" if cat else how
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass
    if cat is None:
        cat, how = classify.classify(a.exch_category, a.text, use_llm=use_llm)
    a.category, a.classified_by = cat, how
    a.materiality, a.reasons = score.score(cat, a.exch_category, a.text, weight, _price_move(a.symbol, a.ts),
                                           settings["price_move_pct"])


def ingest_announcements(days: int = 3, symbols: list[str] | None = None, use_llm: bool = True) -> dict:
    settings = get_settings()
    symbols = symbols or portfolio_symbols()
    to, frm = dt.date.today(), dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=days)
    stats = {"fetched": 0, "new": 0, "enriched": 0, "errors": []}
    for sym in symbols:
        try:
            rows = nse.announcements(sym, frm, to)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            stats["errors"].append(f"{sym}: {e}")
            continue
        stats["fetched"] += len(rows)
        with session() as s:
            weight = (s.get(Company, sym).weight if s.get(Company, sym) else 0) or 0
            for r in rows:
                if s.get(Announcement, r["id"]):
                    continue
                a = Announcement(**r)
                process(a, weight, settings, use_llm)
                s.add(a)
                stats["new"] += 1
    stats["enriched"] = enrich_pending(use_llm=use_llm)
    return stats


def enrich_pending(limit: int = 60, use_llm: bool = True) -> int:
    """Enrich material announcements that have no enrichment yet, or whose results numbers were pending."""
    with session() as s:
        cands = list(s.scalars(select(Announcement).where(Announcement.materiality >= 45)
                               .order_by(Announcement.ts.desc()).limit(400)))
    n = 0
    for a in cands:
        e = a.enrichment or {}
        needs = (a.enriched_at is None or e.get("status") in ("pending", "llm_unavailable", "fallback")
                 and (now() - a.enriched_at) > dt.timedelta(minutes=30))
        if not needs or (not use_llm and a.category != "results"):
            continue
        try:

"""Triggered alerts, evaluated on read against the user's current thresholds.

Price: |daily return| ≥ X%  (also reports the move in σ of the stock's own recent volatility)
Volume: volume ≥ k × trailing N-day average
Announcement: category in the user's watch-list and materiality ≥ threshold
Price/volume alerts are linked to a same-session filing when one exists — "volume 3× · results filed 15:42".
"""
import datetime as dt
import statistics

from sqlalchemy import select

from ..db import Announcement, Company, session
from ..sources.prices import history

MARKET_CLOSE = dt.time(15, 30)


def _session_date(ts: dt.datetime, trading_days: list[dt.date]) -> dt.date | None:
    """The trading session in which the market could first react to a filing made at `ts`."""
    d = ts.date() if ts.time() < MARKET_CLOSE else ts.date() + dt.timedelta(days=1)
    for t in trading_days:
        if t >= d:
            return t
    return None


def eod_moves(symbol: str, settings: dict, days: int = 7) -> list[dict]:
    override = (settings.get("overrides") or {}).get(symbol, {})
    pct_th = override.get("price_move_pct", settings["price_move_pct"])
    vol_th = override.get("volume_multiple", settings["volume_multiple"])
    look = settings["volume_lookback_days"]
    rows = history(symbol, look + days + 5)
    out = []
    for i in range(max(look + 1, len(rows) - days), len(rows)):
        cur, prev = rows[i], rows[i - 1]
        window = rows[i - look:i]
        rets = [window[j].close / window[j - 1].close - 1 for j in range(1, len(window))]
        sigma = statistics.pstdev(rets) if len(rets) > 5 else None
        ret = cur.close / prev.close - 1
        avg_vol = statistics.fmean([w.volume for w in window if w.volume]) if window else None
        mult = cur.volume / avg_vol if avg_vol and cur.volume else None
        z = ret / sigma if sigma else None
        base = {"symbol": symbol, "date": cur.date.isoformat(), "close": round(cur.close, 2),
                "ret_pct": round(ret * 100, 2), "sigma": round(z, 1) if z is not None else None,
                "vol_mult": round(mult, 2) if mult else None, "volume": cur.volume}
        if abs(ret) * 100 >= pct_th:
            out.append({**base, "kind": "price", "threshold": pct_th,
                        "title": f"{symbol} {ret * 100:+.1f}% to ₹{cur.close:,.2f}"
                                 + (f" · {abs(z):.1f}σ move" if z is not None else "")})
        if mult and mult >= vol_th:
            out.append({**base, "kind": "volume", "threshold": vol_th,
                        "title": f"{symbol} volume {mult:.1f}× its {look}-day average"
                                 + f" · price {ret * 100:+.1f}%"})
    return out


def compute(settings: dict, days: int = 7) -> list[dict]:
    with session() as s:
        symbols = list(s.scalars(select(Company.symbol).where(Company.in_portfolio)))
        since = dt.datetime.now() - dt.timedelta(days=days + 3)
        anns = list(s.scalars(select(Announcement).where(Announcement.ts >= since, Announcement.symbol.in_(symbols))))
    alerts = []
    for sym in symbols:
        trading = [r.date for r in history(sym, 40)]
        moves = eod_moves(sym, settings, days)
        sym_anns = [a for a in anns if a.symbol == sym and a.materiality >= 25]
        for m in moves:
            d = dt.date.fromisoformat(m["date"])
            linked = [a for a in sym_anns if _session_date(a.ts, trading) == d]
            linked.sort(key=lambda a: -a.materiality)
            if linked:
                a = linked[0]
                m["linked"] = {"id": a.id, "category": a.category, "ts": a.ts.isoformat(), "text": a.summary or a.text}
            m["id"] = f"{m['kind']}:{sym}:{m['date']}"
            alerts.append(m)
    cutoff = dt.datetime.now() - dt.timedelta(days=days)
    for a in anns:
        if a.ts >= cutoff and a.category in settings["alert_categories"] and a.materiality >= settings["min_alert_materiality"]:
            alerts.append({"id": f"ann:{a.id}", "kind": "announcement", "symbol": a.symbol, "date": a.ts.date().isoformat(),
                           "ts": a.ts.isoformat(), "category": a.category, "materiality": a.materiality,
                           "title": f"{a.symbol} · {a.category.replace('_', ' ')}", "announcement_id": a.id,
                           "text": a.summary or a.text})
    alerts.sort(key=lambda x: (x["date"], x.get("ts", "")), reverse=True)
    return alerts

import re

BASE = {
    "results": 80, "M&A": 72, "fund_raise": 65, "management_change": 45, "litigation": 68, "insider_trading": 45,
    "earnings_call": 25, "investor_meetings": 12, "credit_rating": 40, "dividend": 38, "bonus_split": 55, "capex": 60,

}

# (category or "*", regex, adjustment, reason). Applied in order; all matches count.
ADJUST = [
    ("results", r"newspaper|publication", -62, "Newspaper ad of results already filed"),

     35, "Top-management role (CEO/MD/CFO/Chair)"),

    ("management_change", r"independent director|non[- ]executive", -10, "Board-level, non-executive role"),
    ("management_change", r"company secretary|compliance officer|senior management personnel|\bsmp\b", -20, "Junior KMP change"),
    ("management_change", r"re-?appoint", -15, "Re-appointment, not a change"),
    ("credit_rating", r"downgrad|negative|watch with negative", 45, "Rating downgrade / negative outlook"),
